Add a blow-up of a region

Source: R/crop-zoom.R
add_zoom.Rd

add_zoom() adds a new view to the montage: an enlarged region of each image, shown as panels of their own. Map view to x or y in the layout to show them next to the main panels, or choose them with layout_grid(view = "zoom"). A box marks the region on the main panels.

Usage

add_zoom(
  montage,
  width,
  height = width,
  center = c(0.5, 0.5),
  units = c("um", "px"),
  center_units = c("rel", "px"),
  name = NULL,
  box = c("all", "merge", "none"),
  label = NULL,
  angle = NULL
)

Arguments

montage

A tidymontage() object.

width, height

Size of the region. In micrometres by default, which keeps the magnification equal even if images have different pixel sizes.

center

Position of the region's center: a numeric vector c(x, y) used for all images, or a data frame with columns x, y and one or more columns of the images tibble to match on, e.g. condition or filepath. The data frame can also have an angle column, for a different angle per image.

units

Units of width and height: "um" (micrometres, needs a known pixel size) or "px" (pixels).

center_units

Units of center: "rel" (relative, 0-1) or "px".

name

Name of the view in the layout. By default "zoom", or "zoom 1", "zoom 2", ... if the montage has several zooms.

box

Where to draw the box that marks the region on the main panels: on "all" panels, only on "merge" panels, or "none".

label

Label shown in the box and in the zoom panels. By default the number of the zoom if the montage has several, otherwise none. A string sets your own label; NA shows none.

angle

Rotation of the region in degrees, counterclockwise, see add_crop(). NULL (the default) takes the angle of the crop, so the zoom box sits square in a rotated crop; 0 keeps the zoom upright.

Value

The montage with the zoom step added.

Details

As for add_crop(), the size is the same for all images, so all blow-ups share one magnification, and positions are centers relative to the full image by default.

Call add_zoom() again for more zooms. With two or more, they are numbered in the order they were added: the number is shown in the top-left corner of each box and of each panel of that zoom, and the views are named "zoom 1", "zoom 2", ... unless name is given.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
montage |>
  add_crop(width = 40) |>
  add_zoom(width = 8, center = c(0.45, 0.6)) |>
  layout_grid(x = channel, y = view)

# two numbered zooms
montage |>
  add_zoom(width = 8, center = c(0.45, 0.6)) |>
  add_zoom(width = 8, center = c(0.7, 0.3))
} # }
